plugins.description: Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Replaces bb's thread list with one Activity list of every parent thread from every project, latest first, with pinned threads above it and the Working, Asleep and Archived shelves folded at its foot. A filter narrows it to one project, and rows are one line or two. Each row shows the thread's agent, its project's coloured initial, its title, its pull request, how many threads run under it, and its state or how long ago it last moved. Right-click a row for bb's own thread menu, with Sleep (or Wake) added; under the pointer, its corner offers Archive. A thread put to sleep waits on Asleep until its time, then comes back to the top. Rest on a row for its card: its state and since when, machine, project, branch, pull request, its plan while it works, and a tree of its subthreads to open.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Run bb threads on on-demand boat.dev sandboxes that stop when idle, resume on the same disk, and start from the boat saved snapshot, environment and size you pick in the composer, with bb's GitHub login or else boat's, and see boat spend, running sandboxes and money left in a New thread card.
Wakes your Grok Bots by webhook when a bb thread needs attention: an open question or approval, a finished turn, or a failure.

Cards under the new-thread composer. The first, Activity, is six months of your merged GitHub PRs as a calendar grid, with the threads you started, PRs merged and lines changed; its data refreshes in the background, so it opens instantly. With PR Reviews installed, its pull requests card sits beside Activity. With Burn installed, a Burn card shows your spend and tokens for the last week or month against the period before.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Browser-style tabs across the top of bb's main panel, each holding a whole split layout. Clicking a tab brings back its panes at their exact sizes, with the same pane focused. + opens a tab on the New thread screen, and × or a middle-click closes one. Each tab is named after its focused pane's thread and shows the initials of the projects open in it. Each pane keeps its own header below the strip.
Agents draw mdxcn figures in chat: callouts, steps, terminals, tables, KPIs, charts, timelines and more, from a fenced block.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Jot a note from anywhere in bb: click Notes in the sidebar footer or press ⇧⌘J, and a Notes popover opens beside the sidebar with your notes and a composer at its bottom. Type and press ⌘↵. Type @ to link a thread, and attach screenshots or recordings by pasting, dropping or clicking 📎. Or highlight text in a reply and choose Add to notes to keep that passage with a link back to its message. The same list is a Notes card on the New thread screen. Click notes to tick them, then delete them, or choose New thread to put them in the new-thread composer as context, from any screen; on a thread page, Send to this thread puts them in that thread's draft instead. They stay on the list, marked In draft, until you send that message, which deletes them. ⌘↵ and ⇧⌘↵ do the same from the list.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. A daily The Office quote above the new-thread composer. One random quote per day from a public quotes API, with the character who said it; the composer and the homepage cards move down to make room.

A PR Reviews app on the left rail that opens in the main pane, keeps bb's thread sidebar visible, and lists your pull requests across every GitHub project, in Authored by me, Needs my review and Recently merged, with stacked pull requests as trees, and opens each one on a page with its whole diff in a file tree and a guided review, written by a review thread, that walks you through the change step by step. Its Summary shows the PR's activity, as GitHub's Conversation tab does, and every diff shows the PR's GitHub review threads where they belong. It posts to GitHub only the review comments, replies and conversation comments you write or pick from the guide, on your click, and changes a pull request's state only from the state pill on its page; review threads never post to GitHub. A card on the new-thread screen shows the PRs waiting on your review, or your own.
Agents answer data with an inline chart, without being asked, using bb's inline visualizations.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Start a regional manager: a long-lived thread that takes on a body of work and hands each piece to a crew thread. Open its panel in the navigation rail and press New: bb's own new-thread composer opens, already set to a fresh worktree and auto permissions, and the goal you type starts the thread. It plans, keeps its memory in a folder of markdown files on the bb server, and starts crews: child threads that each work on their own branch, on its provider and model unless you pick others, from its brief and done-criteria, with the crew rules and the memory index in their first message. Told to propose crews and wait, it saves them as drafts instead, for you to edit and start. It messages, reads and closes its crews, and sets itself reminders, once or repeating (in two hours, at a time, every day), that wake it with its own note when they come due; it can list and cancel them. When only you can decide something, it puts a one-line question with up to five options on its board and keeps working: you choose an option or answer in your own words there, never in a form in its thread, and the panel's rail entry counts it with every crew under Needs you on the boards the panel lists. A crew ends its work with one handoff (done, blocked or gave up, with what it did, its evidence, concerns, deviations and findings), stored whole. Every done handoff is checked by an independent verifier the plugin starts itself: a hidden thread in the crew's environment, on another model when bb has one, that runs what proves each done-criterion and returns a verdict with the output as evidence. The plugin itself checks that the claimed commit is checked out on a clean tree, reading the crew's environment through bb's git plugin as it hands off, never through the verifier's shell: anything else fails the verdict, and a read bb can't make leaves it unverified, with no fix round spent. When the crew has a pull request, a verdict that passed every criterion waits under Verifying until CI finishes on the claimed commit, and fails if CI fails. A crew's first failed verdict goes straight back to it: the plugin sends each failed criterion and its evidence to the crew's thread as a message from the verifier, and the crew fixes it and hands off again for a new check. A second failure goes to the regional manager, which messages the crew, asks you, or replaces it with a fresh crew that starts from its brief and its latest findings. The plugin then wakes the regional manager with a short message that names what happened and never quotes a crew; a done handoff reaches it only with its verdict, and its catch-up returns every update in full. It is also woken when a crew fails, waits on you or stops without a handoff, when a crew's pull request opens, merges or closes, its CI passes or fails, or a review approves it or asks for changes (read through gh every minute while CI runs, else every five), when you save a memory file, switch verification or answer one of its questions, and when one of its reminders comes due. A switch on the New page and on the board turns verification off for one regional manager, for handoffs made after it. Its Board, a tab in the thread and a page in the panel, shows that switch, why PR status is unavailable when gh can't read GitHub, its digest, its open decisions under Needs you and answered ones under Done, and every crew under Needs you, Ready for review, Verifying, Working, Landing, Idle or Done, live, each linked to its thread and to its pull request with its CI; a verified handoff waits under Ready for review with ✓, or under Landing while its pull request is open, a merged one is Done, one that failed again after its fix round or couldn't be verified under Needs you with ✗ or the reason, each with its verdict a click away (every criterion, its result and evidence, and the verifier's model), an unchecked one as Unverified, a blocked one under Needs you, and a draft under Needs you with Start and Edit, which opens its brief, model and environment in bb's composer and its done-criteria as a list. bb can't stop the regional manager from editing files itself, so the plugin detects it: when one of its turns ends with changed files in its own environment's working tree, read through bb's git plugin, its board shows a warning and the thread is woken to hand the change to a crew, once per number of changed files; a turn that ends with the tree clean clears the warning. It is detection, not a guarantee: a change it committed isn't seen, and nothing is blocked or reverted. Each row in the panel also opens a Memory editor over the same files; every write names the version it replaces, so neither you nor the thread can silently overwrite the other. Unsaved Memory edits and unsent answers to its questions stay in the browser, through a resize or a reload, until you save or send them.

A live strip above the composer that counts the latest prompt's subagents and child threads, plus any still running, and how long they have taken, and opens into one row per subagent that expands to its report and latest steps and opens its full transcript in the side panel or its own thread; a Subagents tab in the side panel lists every subagent in the thread, grouped by the prompt it was launched after.
